Introduction to Numbers.q: Riya has 8 marbles and her friend has 240 marbles. Which collection is the "large number" one, and why?
Introduction to Numbers.hint: Count the digits in each number — the one with more digits is the larger one.
solution: More digits = bigger number, so 240 is large and 8 is small.

Comparing Numbers.q: A school library has 3,482 books. A city library has 3,847 books. Which library has more books?
Comparing Numbers.hint: Both numbers have the same digit count — compare digit by digit from the left.
Comparing Numbers.answer: The city library (3,847) has more books.
solution: Both numbers have 4 digits, so compare left to right.
So 3,847 > 3,482 — the city library has more books.

Forming Numbers.q: Using the digits 6, 2, 9, and 4 (each once), what is the greatest number you can form?
Forming Numbers.hint: To get the greatest number, place digits from biggest to smallest.
solution: Arrange the digits in descending order: 9, 6, 4, 2.
This is the greatest possible arrangement of these digits.

Indian & International Number System.q: A company earned ₹45,67,890 this year. How would this amount be written using the International number system?
Indian & International Number System.hint: International system groups digits in 3s from the right, unlike the Indian system's 3-2-2 pattern.
solution: Indian system: 45,67,890 (grouped 2-2-3 from left, or 3-2-2 from right).
Regroup in 3s from the right for International style: 4,567,890.

Estimation & Rounding Off.q: A stadium has 68,247 seats. Round this number to the nearest thousand for a news report.
Estimation & Rounding Off.hint: To round to the nearest thousand, check the hundreds digit.
solution: Rounding place: thousands. Check the digit right after it — the hundreds digit.
2 is less than 5, so round down.

Estimating Operations.q: Aarav buys a bicycle for ₹4,890 and a helmet for ₹610. Estimate the total amount he spent.
Estimating Operations.hint: Round each price to the nearest hundred (or thousand) before adding.

Use of Brackets.q: A shop sells notebooks in packs. Each pack has (5 + 3) notebooks, and there are 6 packs. How many notebooks in total?
Use of Brackets.hint: Solve what's inside the brackets first, then multiply.
solution: Solve the bracket first: 5 + 3 = 8 notebooks per pack.
Multiply by the number of packs: 8 × 6.

Roman Numerals.q: A clock face shows the number "IX" where the 9 usually is. What number does IX represent?
Roman Numerals.hint: Look at which symbol comes first — is it smaller or larger than the one after it?
solution: I (smaller) comes before X (larger), so we subtract.

Whole Numbers & the Number Line.q: Priya says "0 is a natural number." Is she right, and why?
Whole Numbers & the Number Line.hint: Natural numbers start counting from 1, not 0.
solution: So 0 is a whole number, but NOT a natural number.

Addition & Subtraction on the Number Lin.q: A frog sits at 4 on a number line. It hops 5 steps forward, then 2 steps back. Where does it land?
Addition & Subtraction on the Number Lin.hint: Forward = move right (add). Back = move left (subtract).

Multiplication & Division on the Number.q: Show how 4 × 3 looks as jumps on a number line, starting from 0.
Multiplication & Division on the Number.hint: Multiplication means equal jumps of the second number, repeated the first number of times.

Closure Property.q: Is the whole number set closed under subtraction? Test it using 3 − 8.
Closure Property.hint: Closure means the answer must always stay a whole number.
solution: −5 is not a whole number (whole numbers start at 0).
Since one case fails, whole numbers are NOT closed under subtraction.

Commutative Property.q: Check whether 27 + 15 gives the same answer as 15 + 27.
Commutative Property.hint: Commutative property says order does not matter for addition.
solution: Both give 42, confirming addition is commutative.

Associative Property.q: Verify that (4 + 6) + 9 gives the same result as 4 + (6 + 9).
Associative Property.hint: Associative property says grouping does not change the sum.
solution: Both equal 19, confirming addition is associative.

Distributive Property.q: A shopkeeper sells 6 boxes, each with (10 + 2) pens. How many pens in total, using the distributive property?
Distributive Property.hint: Distribute the outside number to each term inside the brackets.

Patterns in Whole Numbers.q: What is the next number in the pattern: 1, 1+3, 1+3+5, 1+3+5+7, ...?
Patterns in Whole Numbers.hint: This is the sum of consecutive odd numbers — it always forms a perfect square.

Factors & Multiples.q: A gardener wants to plant 18 saplings in equal rows. What are all the possible ways to arrange them in equal rows (using factor pairs)?
solution: Each pair gives a valid equal-row arrangement.

Divisibility Rules.q: Without dividing, check if 4,536 is divisible by 3 and by 9.
Divisibility Rules.hint: Add all the digits, then check if the sum is divisible by 3 and by 9.
solution: So 4,536 is divisible by both 3 and 9.

Prime & Composite Numbers.q: Is 51 a prime number? Justify your answer.
Prime & Composite Numbers.hint: Check if 51 has any factors other than 1 and itself.
solution: Try dividing 51 by small numbers: 51 ÷ 3 = 17 exactly.
So 51 has factors 1, 3, 17, 51 — more than 2 factors.
Since it has more than 2 factors, 51 is composite, not prime.

Prime Factorization.hint: Keep dividing by the smallest possible prime number until you reach 1.

HCF and LCM.q: Two bells ring every 12 minutes and every 18 minutes. If they ring together now, after how many minutes will they ring together again?
HCF and LCM.hint: This is asking for the LCM of 12 and 18.
solution: So they will ring together again after 36 minutes.

Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.q: Find the HCF of 24 and 36 using prime factorization.
Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.hint: Take the common primes at their lowest powers.
solution: Common primes with lowest powers: 2² and 3¹.

Points, Lines & Line Segments.q: A carpenter marks two points on a plank and joins them with a straight cut that stops at both marks. What geometric figure did the carpenter create?
Points, Lines & Line Segments.hint: A figure with two fixed endpoints and a measurable length.
solution: The cut has a clear start point and end point.
It does not extend beyond either mark.
A straight path with two fixed endpoints is called a line segment.

Rays.q: A torch is switched on at point A and its light travels in a straight line through point B, continuing forever. What geometric figure represents this light beam?
Rays.hint: This figure has one fixed starting point and extends endlessly in one direction.
solution: The light starts at a fixed point (A) — that is the starting point.
It travels endlessly in one direction through B.
A figure with a fixed start and one-direction infinite extension is a ray, named ray AB.

Intersecting & Parallel Lines.q: Two roads are drawn on a map. They are always exactly 2 km apart and never meet, however far they are extended. What type of lines are these roads?
Intersecting & Parallel Lines.hint: Lines that always stay the same distance apart are a specific type.
solution: The roads never meet, no matter how far extended.
They maintain a constant distance (2 km) throughout.
Lines that never meet and stay equidistant are called parallel lines.

Curves — Open & Closed.q: Meera draws the path of an ant which starts at point A and ends at a different point B, never crossing itself. Is this an open or closed curve?
Curves — Open & Closed.hint: Check whether the starting and ending points are the same.
solution: The ant's path starts at A and ends at B (different points).
Since the start and end points are not the same, it does not enclose a region.
A curve that does not start and end at the same point is an open curve.

Polygons.q: A garden is shaped with 5 straight boundary walls, forming a closed figure. What type of polygon is this garden, and how many vertices does it have?
Polygons.hint: Count of sides tells you the polygon name; vertices = sides for any polygon.
solution: 5 straight sides forming a closed figure = a polygon with 5 sides.
A 5-sided polygon is called a pentagon.
Number of vertices always equals number of sides, so it has 5 vertices.

Angles & Their Parts.q: Two rays start from the same point O and open out to form a shape. What is this common starting point O called?
Angles & Their Parts.hint: This point is where both arms of an angle meet.
solution: An angle is formed by two rays sharing a common starting point.
That shared starting point is called the vertex.
So point O is the vertex of the angle.

Triangles.q: A signboard is shaped like a closed figure with exactly 3 straight sides and 3 corners. What shape is the signboard, and how many angles does it have?
Triangles.hint: Count of sides = count of angles for any polygon.
solution: 3 straight sides forming a closed figure = a triangle (the simplest polygon).
A triangle always has exactly 3 vertices.
Since each vertex forms one angle, it has 3 angles.

Quadrilaterals.q: A kite-shaped playground has 4 straight sides and 4 corners. How many diagonals does this playground have?
Quadrilaterals.hint: A quadrilateral always has exactly 2 diagonals (connecting non-adjacent vertices).
solution: A quadrilateral has 4 vertices, e.g. A, B, C, D.
Diagonals connect non-adjacent vertices: AC and BD.

Circles.q: A circular pizza has a radius of 12 cm. What is the length of the longest possible straight cut through its center?
Circles.hint: The longest chord of a circle is its diameter, which equals 2 × radius.
solution: The longest straight cut through the center (diameter) is 24 cm.

Measuring Line Segments.q: Using a divider, Ravi transfers the length of a line segment onto his ruler and reads 8.5 cm. What is the actual length of the line segment?
Measuring Line Segments.hint: A divider transfers the exact length without misreading — the ruler reading IS the length.
solution: The divider was opened to match the segment's two endpoints exactly.
This exact opening was then placed on the ruler without changing it.
So the ruler reading directly gives the segment's length: 8.5 cm.

Angles & Their Types.q: A door is opened so that it makes an angle of 130° with the wall. Classify this angle.
Angles & Their Types.hint: Check if the angle is less than 90°, between 90° and 180°, or between 180° and 360°.
solution: 130° is greater than 90° but less than 180°.
Angles in this range are called obtuse angles.
So the door makes an obtuse angle with the wall.

Measuring Angles.q: While measuring an angle with a protractor, one arm is at the 0° line and the other arm crosses at the 55° mark. What is the angle's measure?
Measuring Angles.hint: Read the mark where the second arm crosses, since the first arm is aligned with 0°.
solution: The baseline (0° line) is aligned with the first arm.
The second arm crosses the scale at 55°.

Perpendicular Lines.q: Two walls of a room meet at a corner, forming a perfect right angle. What term describes the relationship between these two walls?
Perpendicular Lines.hint: Lines meeting at exactly 90° have a special name.
solution: The two walls meet and form an angle of exactly 90°.
Lines (or surfaces) that intersect at exactly 90° are called perpendicular.
So the two walls are perpendicular to each other.

Classification of Triangles.q: A triangle has sides measuring 7 cm, 7 cm, and 10 cm. Classify this triangle by its sides.
Classification of Triangles.hint: Check how many sides are equal.
solution: Two sides are equal: 7 cm and 7 cm.
The third side (10 cm) is different.
A triangle with exactly 2 equal sides is called isosceles.

Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.q: A quadrilateral has all 4 sides equal, but its angles are 80° and 100° (not 90°). What shape is it?
Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.hint: Equal sides with non-right angles matches a specific quadrilateral type.
solution: All 4 sides are equal — this rules out a general quadrilateral.
But the angles are not 90°, so it is not a square.
A shape with all equal sides but angles that aren't 90° is a rhombus.

Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.q: A stop sign has 8 equal sides and 8 equal angles. What is this polygon called, and is it regular or irregular?
Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.hint: Count the sides to name the polygon, then check if all sides/angles are equal.
solution: All sides AND all angles are equal, so it meets both conditions for "regular."

Circle Parts.q: A circular table has a diameter of 90 cm. What is its radius?
Circle Parts.hint: Radius is half of the diameter.
solution: So the table's radius is 45 cm.

3D Shapes.q: A box of chocolates is shaped like a rectangular block. How many faces, edges, and vertices does it have?
3D Shapes.hint: This shape is called a cuboid — recall its standard face/edge/vertex counts.
solution: A rectangular block is called a cuboid.
A cuboid always has 6 rectangular faces.
It has 12 edges and 8 vertices (corner points).

Representing Integers.q: A submarine is positioned 250 m below sea level. How is this position represented as an integer?
Representing Integers.hint: Below a reference point (sea level) is represented using negative integers.
solution: Sea level is the reference point, treated as 0.
Below sea level means moving in the negative direction.
250 m below sea level is represented as −250.

Integers on the Number Line.q: On a number line, which integer is further to the left: −6 or −2?
Integers on the Number Line.hint: More negative numbers are always further to the left.
solution: On a number line, more negative numbers sit further left.
So −6 is to the left of −2.

Addition of Integers.q: The temperature was −4°C in the morning. It rose by 9°C by afternoon. What was the afternoon temperature?
Addition of Integers.hint: A rise means adding to the current temperature.
solution: Different signs — subtract smaller from larger: 9 − 4 = 5, and 9 has the bigger value (positive).

Subtraction of Integers.q: The temperature was 3°C. It then dropped by a further 8°C, and later increased when accounting for a −5°C recorded error being removed. Find 3 − (−5).
Subtraction of Integers.hint: Subtracting a negative number means adding its positive value.

Ordering Integers.q: Arrange these temperatures in ascending order: 4°C, −7°C, 0°C, −2°C, 6°C.
Ordering Integers.hint: Ascending means smallest to largest — most negative numbers come first.
solution: Then positives smallest to largest: 4, then 6.

Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.q: A hiker starts at an elevation of 0 m, climbs 45 m, then descends 60 m. What is the hiker's final elevation relative to the start?
Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.hint: Climbing = positive change, descending = negative change. Combine them.
solution: Final elevation is −15 m (15 m below the starting point).

Types of Fractions.q: A cake is cut into 8 equal slices. Aman eats 3 slices. What fraction of the cake did he eat?
Types of Fractions.hint: Numerator = parts taken, denominator = total equal parts.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: A recipe needs 11/4 cups of flour. Express this as a mixed number.
Proper & Improper Fractions.hint: Divide the numerator by the denominator; the remainder becomes the new numerator.

Fractions on Number Line.q: Where would you mark 3/5 on a number line between 0 and 1?
Fractions on Number Line.hint: Divide the space into as many equal parts as the denominator, then count to the numerator.
Fractions on Number Line.answer: At the 3rd of 5 equal divisions between 0 and 1.
solution: Denominator (5) tells us to divide the segment from 0 to 1 into 5 equal parts.
Numerator (3) tells us to count to the 3rd division mark.

Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.hint: Divide both numerator and denominator by their HCF.

Comparing Fractions.hint: Convert both fractions to a common denominator (their LCM) before comparing.

Fraction of a Quantity.q: A class has 40 students. If 3/8 of them play football, how many students play football?
Fraction of a Quantity.hint: "Of" means multiply the fraction by the total quantity.

Addition & Subtraction of Fractions.hint: Find a common denominator (LCM) before adding.

Word Problems / Mixed Practice.q: A tank is 3/4 full of water. If 1/4 of the tank's capacity leaks out, what fraction of the tank is now full?
Word Problems / Mixed Practice.hint: Subtract the leaked fraction from the starting fraction.
solution: So the tank is now 1/2 full.

Tenths & Hundredths.q: A ribbon is 7/10 metres long. Write this length as a decimal.
Tenths & Hundredths.hint: A fraction with denominator 10 converts directly to one decimal digit.
solution: Write 7 in the first position after the decimal point.

Place Value & Expanded Form of Decimals.hint: Multiply each digit by its correct place value, then add.

Decimals on the Number Line.q: Where would 0.6 be located between 0 and 1 on a number line?
Decimals on the Number Line.hint: Divide the space between 0 and 1 into 10 equal parts (tenths).
Decimals on the Number Line.answer: At the 6th of 10 equal divisions between 0 and 1.
solution: Divide the segment from 0 to 1 into 10 equal parts.

Comparing Decimals.hint: Compare digit by digit from left to right, starting with the whole number part.

Converting Fractions ↔ Decimals.hint: Divide the numerator by the denominator.

Using Decimals in Money & Length.q: Meena buys items worth ₹45.50 and ₹14.75. What is the total cost?
Using Decimals in Money & Length.hint: Align the decimal points, then add as usual.

Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.hint: Align decimal points, padding with zeros if needed, then subtract.

Word Problems on Decimals.q: Rahul has ₹150.50. He spends ₹67.25 on a book. How much money does he have left?
Word Problems on Decimals.hint: Subtract the amount spent from the amount he started with.

Fill in the Blanks & True/False Practice.q: True or False: 0.5 and 0.50 represent the same value.
Fill in the Blanks & True/False Practice.hint: Trailing zeros after a decimal do not change its value.
solution: Trailing zeros added after the last decimal digit do not change the value.

Introduction to Data Handling.q: A teacher records the marks of 30 students in a test, one by one, in the order they submit their papers. What kind of data is this before any organizing is done?
Introduction to Data Handling.hint: Unorganized, freshly collected data has a specific name.
solution: The marks are collected in original order, not yet sorted or grouped.
Data in this unorganized, original form is called raw data.

Recording Data.q: A researcher wants to find out students' favorite sports by asking each of them directly. What data collection method is this?
Recording Data.hint: Asking people questions to gather responses has a specific name.
solution: The researcher is directly asking individuals for their responses.
Collecting data by asking questions is called a survey.

Tally Marks.q: A survey shows tally marks with 3 complete groups of 5, plus 2 extra strokes for "blue" as a favorite color. How many students chose blue?

Organizing Data in Tables.q: A frequency table shows: Apples = 8, Bananas = 5, Mangoes = 12. What is the total number of fruits recorded?
Organizing Data in Tables.hint: Add up all the frequencies in the table.

Pictographs.q: In a pictograph, 🚗 = 5 cars. If a row shows 4 car symbols, how many cars does that row represent?
Pictographs.hint: Multiply the number of symbols by the value each symbol represents.

Interpreting Pictographs.q: If 📘 = 4 books, and a category shows 2.5 book symbols, how many books does that represent?
Interpreting Pictographs.hint: Multiply the symbol count (including partial symbols) by the key value.

Bar Graphs.q: On a bar graph, each gridline represents 10 units. A bar reaches the 3rd gridline. What value does this bar represent?
Bar Graphs.hint: Multiply the gridline number by the value each gridline represents.
solution: So the bar represents a value of 30.

Interpreting Bar Graphs.q: Bar A shows a value of 45, and Bar B shows a value of 30 on a bar graph. What is the difference between them?
Interpreting Bar Graphs.hint: Subtract the smaller value from the larger value.
solution: The difference between Bar A and Bar B is 15.

Comparing Data.q: Team A scored 85 runs and Team B scored 92 runs. Which team scored more, and by how much?
Comparing Data.hint: Compare the two values, then find the difference.
solution: Compare: 92 > 85, so Team B scored more.
Team B scored 7 runs more than Team A.

Word Problems on Data Handling.q: A pictograph shows 🍎 = 5 apples per symbol. A row has 6 symbols. How many apples were sold?
Word Problems on Data Handling.hint: Multiply the number of symbols by the value per symbol.

Fill in the Blanks & True/False.q: True or False: A pictograph can be correctly read without checking its key.
Fill in the Blanks & True/False.hint: The key tells you what value each symbol represents.
solution: The key (legend) defines what each symbol stands for.
Without checking it, the pictograph cannot be interpreted correctly.

Introduction to Perimeter.q: A rectangular field has sides 10 m, 15 m, 10 m, and 15 m. Find its perimeter.
Introduction to Perimeter.hint: Add up all the side lengths.

Perimeter of Regular Shapes.q: Find the perimeter of a regular hexagon with each side measuring 9 cm.
Perimeter of Regular Shapes.hint: For a regular polygon, Perimeter = number of sides × one side length.

Perimeter of a Rectangle.q: A rectangular garden is 15 m long and 9 m wide. Find its perimeter.

Perimeter of a Square.q: Find the perimeter of a square park with each side measuring 14 m.

Perimeter of a Triangle.q: A triangular plot has sides 7 m, 9 m, and 11 m. Find its perimeter.

Introduction to Area.q: Why must area always be expressed in square units, like cm² or m², instead of just cm or m?
Introduction to Area.hint: Area measures 2-dimensional space, not just one length.
Introduction to Area.answer: Because area covers 2 dimensions (length and width).
solution: Area represents the surface covered by a shape, involving both length and width.
Measuring two dimensions together requires square units.
So area is always expressed as cm², m², etc.

Area of a Rectangle.q: A rectangular room is 6 m long and 4 m wide. Find its area.

Area of a Square.q: Find the area of a square plot with each side measuring 11 m.

Area of Irregular Shapes.q: An L-shaped room is made of a 4m × 3m rectangle and a 2m × 2m square. Find its total area.
Area of Irregular Shapes.hint: Split the shape into known shapes, find each area, then add.

Perimeter and Area in Real Life.q: A square park has a side of 25 m. Find the cost of fencing it if the rate is ₹20 per metre.
Perimeter and Area in Real Life.hint: First find the perimeter, then multiply by the cost per metre.

Word Problems on Mensuration.q: A rectangular field is 30 m by 20 m. Find both its perimeter and area.
Word Problems on Mensuration.hint: Use the rectangle perimeter and area formulas separately.

Fill in the Blanks & True/False: Mensura.q: True or False: Area and perimeter are always measured in the same units.
Fill in the Blanks & True/False: Mensura.hint: Perimeter is a length; area is a surface. Do they use the same type of units?
solution: Perimeter uses length units, like cm or m.
Area uses square units, like cm² or m².
Since these are different types of units, the statement is False.

Introduction to Algebra.q: A shop sells notebooks at ₹15 each. Write an algebraic expression for the cost of "n" notebooks.
Introduction to Algebra.hint: Multiply the price per notebook by the number of notebooks.

Matchstick Patterns.q: A single square is made using 4 matchsticks. Each additional connected square (sharing one side) uses 3 more matchsticks. How many matchsticks are needed for 4 squares in a row?
Matchstick Patterns.hint: First square = 4 sticks; each new one afterward adds 3 more.
solution: Each additional square adds 3: for 3 more squares, that's 3 × 3 = 9.

The Idea of a Variable.q: In the expression "x + 8", identify the variable and the constant.
The Idea of a Variable.hint: The variable can change; the constant stays fixed.
solution: x can represent different values — it is the variable.
8 is a fixed number — it is the constant.

Rules from Geometry.q: Write the algebraic rule for the perimeter of an equilateral triangle with side "a".
Rules from Geometry.hint: All three sides are equal, so add the side three times.

Rules from Arithmetic.q: Write the commutative property of multiplication using variables.
Rules from Arithmetic.hint: This property says the order of multiplication doesn't matter.
solution: Commutative property means order doesn't change the result.
For multiplication, this is written as a × b = b × a.

Expressions with Variables.q: Write an algebraic expression for "7 more than three times a number x."
Expressions with Variables.hint: "Three times a number" means 3x; "7 more than" means add 7.

Value of an Expression.q: Find the value of "3p − q" when p = 4 and q = 7.
Value of an Expression.hint: Substitute the given values, then simplify using order of operations.

Using Expressions Practically.q: A taxi charges ₹50 plus ₹8 per km. Write an expression for the total fare for "d" km, then find the fare for 12 km.

What is an Equation?.q: Write an equation for: "Five times a number is 45."
What is an Equation?.hint: "Five times a number" is 5x; "is" means equals.

Solving an Equation.hint: Subtract 7 from both sides to isolate x.

Word Problems on Algebra.q: A number decreased by 9 equals 14. Find the number.
Word Problems on Algebra.hint: Set up an equation with the unknown number, then solve.

Fill in the Blanks & True/False: Algebra.q: True or False: An expression can be "solved" the same way an equation can.
Fill in the Blanks & True/False: Algebra.hint: Expressions have no equals sign — can they be solved for a specific value?
solution: An equation has an "=" sign and can be solved for the variable's value.
An expression has no "=" sign — it can only be evaluated or simplified, not solved.
